applicable_when: Matrix B has strides (stride_bk=1, stride_bn=480), meaning K is the fast (contiguous) dimension in memory and N is the slow (strided) dimension. The current make_block_ptr for B uses order=(0, 1), which tells the TMA hardware that dim-1 (N) is the fastest-varying dimension — the opposite of reality. This causes every B tile load to access memory with 480-float (1920-byte) strides between consecutive N elements, producing severely uncoalesced global loads and then strided writes into shared memory that cause 5.3-way bank conflicts. The fix is to change B_block_ptr order from (0, 1) to (1, 0), which correctly declares K (dim-0) as the contiguous dimension, enabling coalesced 128-byte sector reads. Additionally, BLOCK_N=128 wastes 25% of every tile since N=96 — reducing BLOCK_N to 96 eliminates masked-out computation and reduces the accumulator size. Prior correctness failures (max_diff~130) were caused by accidentally enabling TF32 in tl.dot(); this plan explicitly preserves allow_tf32=False throughout.

strategy_title: Increasing BLOCK_K Doubles Shared Memory, Kills Occupancy
strategy_description: Changing BLOCK_K from 32 to 64 while keeping BLOCK_N=128 (or changing to 96) doubled the dynamic shared memory per block from 65 KB to 131 KB, causing Block Limit Shared Mem to drop from 3 to 1. This halved theoretical occupancy from 12.5% to 6.25%, reduced active warps/scheduler from 2.0 to 1.0, and collapsed eligible warps/scheduler from 0.75 to 0.09 — causing 91.3% of cycles to have no eligible warp (up from 58.8%). The kernel duration increased 6x (3.39ms → 20.87ms). When shared memory per block is already near the per-SM limit, increasing BLOCK_K to improve arithmetic intensity will instead destroy occupancy by making Block Limit Shared Mem the binding constraint.
slow_pseudocode:
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 32
BLOCK_N : tl.constexpr = 128
# dynamic_smem = A_tile + B_tile = 128*32*4 + 32*128*4 = 32KB + 32KB = 64KB
# Block Limit Shared Mem = 3 -> Theoretical Occupancy = 12.5%
fast_pseudocode:
# DO NOT DO THIS when smem is already near limit:
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 64
BLOCK_N : tl.constexpr = 96
# dynamic_smem = 128*64*4 + 64*96*4 = 32KB + 24KB = 56KB... but actual measured = 131KB
# Block Limit Shared Mem = 1 -> Theoretical Occupancy = 6.25% (WORSE)
applicable_when: Never apply this specific change (BLOCK_K 32->64 in this kernel configuration). As a general signal: when dynamic shared memory per block is already ≥50% of the per-SM shared memory budget, increasing tile dimensions that grow shared memory will reduce Block Limit Shared Mem and hurt occupancy.
do_not_apply_when: Do not increase BLOCK_K when the kernel is already near the shared memory per-SM limit. The before state had 65KB/block with Block Limit Shared Mem=3; doubling BLOCK_K pushed it to 131KB/block with Block Limit Shared Mem=1, causing a 6x slowdown. This pattern is harmful whenever shared memory is the binding occupancy constraint.
framework_notes: Triton on H200 (SM 9.0). The shared memory configuration size is 233KB/SM. With 131KB dynamic + 1KB driver = 132KB/block, only 1 block fits per SM. The stack size also tripled (1024 → 3072), suggesting the compiler spilled more to local memory due to the larger tile, compounding the regression.
